steps.message:
I scanned only the production source of `ObjExclusion/` and deliberately skipped the `obj/` and `bin/` directories, which hold auto-generated build output rather than code you maintain. Two production `.cs` files were in scope: `Services/DataService.cs` and `Program.cs`.

### Static dependencies in production source (needs wrapping)

| File:line | Call | Category | Replacement |
|-----------|------|----------|-------------|
| Services/DataService.cs:7 | `DateTime.UtcNow` | Time | TimeProvider |
| Services/DataService.cs:9 | `Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("OUTPUT_DIR")` | Environment | IEnvironmentProvider |
| Services/DataService.cs:12 | `File.WriteAllText` | File System | System.IO.Abstractions |
| Services/DataService.cs:14 | `Console.WriteLine` | Console | ILogger |
| Services/DataService.cs:19 | `Directory.GetFiles` | File System | System.IO.Abstractions |
| Services/DataService.cs:22 | `File.ReadAllText` | File System | System.IO.Abstractions |
| Program.cs:7 | `Console.WriteLine` | Console | ILogger |

`Path.Combine` on DataService.cs:8 is a pure helper and needs no seam.

### Excluded

The `obj/` and `bin/` trees also contain statics, but they live in tool-generated files that are recreated on every build. Wrapping them would be pointless and they are correctly left out of the totals above.

### Recommendation

Start with the three File System calls in `DataService.cs` behind `IFileSystem`, then inject `TimeProvider` for the timestamp and an environment seam for `OUTPUT_DIR`.
